name: Imperial Military

source_refs.source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook
source_refs.content: The Imperial Military section: Navy as backbone, Army surface ops, Stormtrooper Corps as a separate branch answering to the Emperor via Stormtrooper Command; Tarkin Doctrine; combined-arms after Yavin; Carida indoctrination.

source_refs.source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook
source_refs.content: Pyramidal Imperial structure, Palpatine at the apex; Tarkin Doctrine and the Grand Moff concept attributed to the late commander of the Death Star.

The Galactic Empire (Military) adversaries section: the military is many arms with bitter rivalries, not one entity; Army surface ops + Vehicle/Gunnery Corps; Stormtrooper Corps an independent branch that can overrule Army/Navy officers; numbers-without-care doctrine; rank opacity ('commander').

Detailed org breakdown: Army (Armor/Artillery, Special Forces, Maritime, Air, Engineering, MP) HQ Coruscant; Navy + Admiralty + Fleet Command, fleets backboned by ~half a dozen Star Destroyers; Starfighter Corps almost all TIEs, numerical not vehicle superiority (3:1 sortie threshold).
Imperial academy system: indoctrination via psychological technique and pharmaceuticals; cadets isolated from support networks; lower-qualified cadets enlist directly as stormtroopers.

overview: The Imperial Military is the armed fist of the New Order — the Army, the Navy, and the Stormtrooper Corps that conquer, blockade, garrison, and pacify on the Emperor's behalf. It is not a single monolith but several rivalrous arms: the Navy is the backbone, its massive fleets backboned by Star Destroyers and administered by the Admiralty and Fleet Command; the Army owns everything that happens on a planet's surface, from walker columns to garrison troops; and the Stormtrooper Corps is a separate branch answering to the Emperor through Stormtrooper Command, the implacable face of Imperial power. (Excludes the political and intelligence organizations — ISB, Imperial Intelligence, and COMPNOR — which are their own branches of the Empire.)
short_descriptor: Overwhelming, doctrinaire, and predictable at scale: it wins by numbers and materiel, not finesse. Individual units are beatable; the system behind them is not.

witness_statement.text: You don't fight the Imperial Military, you survive it. They blockade from orbit, drop stormtroopers to take the ground, and bury mistakes under more hardware. The trick isn't beating a squad — it's being somewhere else when the Star Destroyer arrives.
witness_statement.verification: in-world GM-voice; mechanics grounded in cited pages

history.heading: ORIGINS
history.text: Forged from the clone armies and starfleet of the Old Republic and re-tooled for occupation, the military became the instrument of the Tarkin Doctrine — rule through fear of overwhelming military might — attributed to the late commander of the Death Star.

history.heading: STORMTROOPERS
history.text: Stormtroopers, once clones, are now recruited and conditioned at facilities such as Carida to recreate the loyalty bred into the originals.

history.heading: INTEGRATION
history.text: After the Death Star's loss at Yavin the Army and Navy integrated into a combined-arms force, every fleet carrying significant ground assets so the Empire can project power to any world.

how_they_operate.heading: THE BLOCKADE PATTERN
how_they_operate.text: The operational pattern is constant: the Navy blockades a world with the firepower of its Star Destroyers, then the Stormtrooper Corps and Army forces invade, establish a beachhead, and occupy.

how_they_operate.heading: GARRISONS AND STARFIGHTERS
how_they_operate.text: The Army garrisons surfaces under sector Moffs; the Starfighter Corps (almost entirely TIE-series craft) commits only when it outnumbers the enemy heavily, trading pilots and hulls freely.

how_they_operate.heading: DOCTRINE
how_they_operate.text: Doctrine prizes numbers and materiel over individual skill: stormtroopers advance without regard for losses, and the mere arrival of the Corps can end a fight before it starts.

motivations.primary: Impose and maintain the Emperor's order through overwhelming, visible force.
motivations.secondary: Out-compete rival Imperial arms for budget, prestige, and command authority.
motivations.notes: The branches' bitter rivalries (Army vs Navy vs Stormtrooper Command) are an exploitable seam.

goals.strategic: Total pacification of the galaxy: blockade, invade, garrison, hold.
goals.operational: Project decisive force to any system faster than resistance can organize.

methods.preferred: Orbital blockade then ground invasion; overwhelming numbers; spectacle of force (the Tarkin Doctrine).
methods.avoided: Finesse, attrition it cannot replace cheaply, and operations that don't read as a show of strength.
methods.notes: Combined-arms since Yavin — fleets carry the Army; the Stormtrooper Corps spearheads.

strengths: Orbital supremacy via Star Destroyer fleets
Stormtrooper Corps shock troops that can take and hold nearly any world
Doctrine of fear that often ends conflicts without combat
weaknesses: Predictable, escalate-by-force doctrine — slow to recognize non-military threats
Bitter inter-branch rivalries create command seams
Numbers over skill: individual troopers are beatable
Reliance on materiel makes losses politically costly (the Death Star)
Rigid top-down chain — local commanders can't improvise when cut off

behavior_under_threat.low: Standard garrison response; a patrol or squad investigates.
behavior_under_threat.medium: Escalate force; lock down transit; call in armor.
behavior_under_threat.high: Commit a fleet element; blockade; deploy stormtrooper legions.
behavior_under_threat.critical: Overwhelming force without regard for collateral or losses; the Tarkin Doctrine in full.

alert_escalation.communication_method: HoloNet and fleet comms up the Moff/High Command chain.
alert_escalation.escalation_speed: Fast once a Star Destroyer is in-system; slow to recognize the threat in the first place.
alert_escalation.chain_of_command: Emperor → Imperial High Command → Grand Moffs → Moffs → local garrison; Stormtrooper Command runs parallel.
alert_escalation.notes: Governors request, they do not command, the Navy.

tension_patterns: Army resents Stormtrooper Corps autonomy to overrule its officers
Navy and Army compete for credit and command of joint operations
Ambitious officers spend lives for visible victories (doctrine of spectacle)
Garrison boredom vs sudden brutal crackdown
Outer Rim deployments stretched thin while the Core stays lightly policed

mcguffin_interest.data: Fleet movements, garrison rosters, blockade schedules.
mcguffin_interest.technology: Starship and walker hardware; captured rebel craft.
mcguffin_interest.notes: Military interest is operational, not ideological — that's ISB/COMPNOR's lane.

presence_by_location_type.command: Sector HQs, Star Destroyer command decks.
presence_by_location_type.covert: Army Special Forces — deniable infiltrators and saboteurs.

regional_presence.outer_rim: Heaviest and most brutal — the frontier of pacification.
regional_presence.unknown_regions: Sparse — Thrawn's Seventh Fleet a notable exception.

relationship_notes.galactic_empire: The Empire's armed instrument; subordinate to the Emperor and High Command.
relationship_notes.imperial_security_bureau: Watched by the ISB for loyalty; resentment runs both ways.
relationship_notes.inquisitorius: Provides muscle for Inquisitor operations; defers on Force matters.

prominent_figures.name: General Maximilian Veers
prominent_figures.notes: Commander of the Blizzard Force walker assault at Hoth — the Army's hammer, the AT-AT made personal.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: A competent, results-driven Army officer in a service full of ideologues. If Veers is running the ground operation, expect armor, method, and no wasted motion.
prominent_figures.wants: Decisive ground victories that prove the Army's worth against a Navy that hogs the credit.
prominent_figures.secret: His professional pride chafes against political officers second-guessing field decisions.

behavior.under_pressure: Methodical escalation — commits armor and presses.
behavior.when_losing: Preserves his force; withdraws rather than waste it on doctrine.
behavior.loyalty: To the Army and to competence; the New Order is the employer.
behavior.tells: Plans around terrain and materiel, not spectacle — unusually pragmatic for an Imperial.

useful_to_players: A pragmatic foe — he respects competent resistance and won't throw lives away chasing a symbol
hooks: An Armor Corps column is mustering for an assault — Veers doesn't deploy walkers for a patrol.

prominent_figures.name: Admiral Firmus Piett
prominent_figures.notes: Rose by surviving where others failed under Vader — a cautious, capable fleet officer who manages risk in a service where failure is fatal.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Piett climbed by not being the one blamed. He runs a tight fleet and avoids the mistakes that get admirals executed — which also makes him cautious and exploitable.
prominent_figures.wants: To survive command under Vader and hold his fleet together.
prominent_figures.secret: He manages the chain of blame as carefully as he manages the fleet.

behavior.when_losing: Protects the fleet and his own position over bold gambits.
behavior.loyalty: To self-preservation within the Navy's lethal hierarchy.
behavior.tells: Hesitates to deliver bad news; hedges commitments.

useful_to_players: His caution can be weaponized — a credible bigger threat will make him redeploy defensively
hooks: A Star Destroyer is holding position instead of pursuing — its admiral is waiting for someone else to take the risk.
